Soon, the city begins demanding that we hurry toward work.

A cracked cup can reveal a vanished household in fragments. Attention resembles an open hand more than a bright spotlight. It lifts what is fragile without demanding explanations from us. It grants small mysteries the time to remain mysterious still. The world becomes richer when we do not rush it. We miss doors opening, clouds changing, bread browning inside bowls.
